category.name: Dynamics & Forces
category.description: Study of forces and their effects on the motion of physical bodies.

lessons.name: Newton's Second Law of Motion
lessons.description: The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass.

variables.name: Net Force
variables.description: Unbalanced force acting on mass (SI unit: N = kg·m/s²)

worked_example.problem: A net force acts on a mass of 5 kg producing an acceleration of 3 m/s². Calculate the force.
steps: Given: mass m = 5 kg, acceleration a = 3 m/s²

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Newton's Second Law quantifies force. One Newton (N) is defined as the force required to accelerate 1 kg at 1 m/s².

lessons.name: Newton's First Law (Inertia)
lessons.description: An object continues in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external net force.

variables.name: Net Force
variables.description: Sum of all external forces acting on object

worked_example.problem: Explain why passengers lurch forward when a bus applies brakes suddenly.
steps: Passengers and bus move together at initial velocity v
Brakes apply retarding force to bus chassis
Due to inertia, passengers' upper bodies tend to maintain constant forward velocity v
Result: Passengers lurch forward relative to bus
worked_example.solution: Inertia resists the state change of passengers.

sections.title: Inertia & Equilibrium
sections.content: Inertia is the natural property of matter to resist any change in state of motion. Mass is the quantitative measure of inertia.

lessons.name: Weight & Gravitational Force
lessons.description: Weight is the force of gravity exerted on a mass by a celestial body.

variables.name: Gravitational Acceleration
variables.description: Acceleration due to gravity (Earth standard g ≈ 9.8 m/s²)

worked_example.problem: Calculate the weight of a 70 kg person on Earth where g = 9.8 m/s².

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Mass is an intrinsic property that remains constant anywhere in the universe, while weight varies with local gravitational field strength g.

lessons.name: Linear Momentum
lessons.description: Quantity of motion possessed by a moving body, equal to the product of its mass and velocity.

variables.name: Linear Momentum
variables.description: Vector quantity of motion (SI unit: kg·m/s)

worked_example.problem: A bullet of mass 0.02 kg is fired with velocity 400 m/s. Find its momentum.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Momentum is a vector quantity. In an isolated system without external forces, total momentum is conserved.
